name: Ukue
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

new_statements.quote: [1989, 4.20.1] Syllable structure: CV, V. ... [4.20.8] Tone: Two significant levels are attested in my data: high and low. In items borrowed from Yoruba, mid tone occurs. || [1973, p. 306] Two significant levels of tone were attested to in Ukue — high and low. There is no evidence of a third level except in certain items which are evidently borrowed. ... A larger corpus of data will be required for a deeper examination of Ukue tones. Note, however, that, as with Ehuẹun and Ibilo, nouns with a low-low tone pattern in the base are high-falling-low on the surface. Thus: /ovie/ 'king' (LLL) → [ôvyè].

new_statements.rule_in_words: Ukue is described as a two-level tone language (High, Low; Mid only in Yoruba loans), syllables CV/V; the only primary descriptions (Elugbe 1973, 1989) say nothing at all about word stress or accent, so no stress placement rule is on record.
new_statements.exceptions: Mid tone occurs only in Yoruba loanwords (e.g. 'God' < Yoruba Ọlọ́run); nouns with underlying L-L(-L) surface as high-falling-low (1973 p. 306). No stress-related exceptions because stress is not discussed.
new_statements.domain_note: Lexical tone on citation forms from one informant (Mr Benjamin Adejube, per 1989 acknowledgments); Elugbe calls his Ukue corpus 'limited'. No statement about word- or phrase-level prominence.
new_statements.identity_note: Elugbe's 'Ukue' (Ukpe, Ikpe) = Ùkùè of Ìpè (and Igbede-Ipe) Akoko, Ondo State = ukue1238 / ISO uku; Olaogun & Oyelade 2025 write 'Ìpè (Ùkùè)'. Glottolog/Wikipedia alt-names 'Epinmi, Ekpenmi' properly belong to the sister lect Ehueun (ehue1238, spoken in Epinmi/Ekpinmi); Elugbe treats Ukue and Ehueun as separate but very close Osse-group languages. Data in both Elugbe sources come from a single Ukue informant.

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Ukue language' (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ukue_language), citing Archangeli & Pulleyblank 1994 and Mielke 2008 (both second-hand from Elugbe)
sources.note: Seven vowels in two harmonic sets, no sibilants, [m n] as allophones of /β l/; nothing on stress or tone placement.

sources.citation: Elugbe, Ben Ohi. 1989. Edoid. In J. Bendor-Samuel (ed.), The Niger-Congo Languages, 291-304. Lanham: University Press of America. [Zenodo 5618102]
sources.note: Lists Ukue (Ukpe, Ikpe) in the Osse group of Northwestern Edoid (p. 296); sec. 13.3.4 Tone systems does not treat Ukue; no stress statement.

sources.citation: Elugbe, Benny Ohiomamhe. 1973. A comparative Edo phonology. PhD thesis, Dept. of Linguistics and Nigerian Languages, University of Ibadan. (Zenodo 4467456 scan = Volume I, 306 pp; Ukue chapter pp. 297-306)
sources.note: Ukue phonemic statement pp. 297-306: syllable structure CV, V (optional glide rule), consonants, vowels (7 oral, 5 nasal), no vowel harmony; sec. 6 Tone p. 306: 'Two significant levels of tone were attested to in Ukue — high and low. There is no evidence of a third level except in certain items which are evidently borrowed... Note, however, that, as with Ehuẹun and Ibilo, nouns with a low-low tone pattern in the base are high-falling-low on the surface.' No mention of stress or accent.
